title: Architecture Standards Reference: API, Coding, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance, and ADRs
author: Aisha Thompson
body:
Overview:
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's canonical architecture and engineering standards covering API design, coding practices, infrastructure and IaC, model-serving requirements, observability expectations, performance benchmarks, and the Decision Record (ADR) workflow. It is intended for engineers, product owners, and architects who are designing or operating services on the Redwood platform.

Purpose and scope:
- Provide a single, actionable set of standards that teams can reference when building new services or updating existing ones.
- Apply to all customer-facing services, backend microservices, and the serving runtime components unless explicitly exempted by an approved ADR.
- Distinguish between normative requirements (must) and recommendations (should/consider).

Ownership and governance:
- Owner team: engineering (platform + infra + runtime).
- Maintenance cadence: quarterly review; ad-hoc updates via ADR where necessary.
- Approval: Platform leads + Security review for infra and data residency changes; Product/PM for public API breaking changes.

1) API Standards (normative unless noted)
- API types and contracts:
  - Public/partner APIs: OpenAPI 3.1-compliant specification required; publish specs in internal API registry.
  - Internal service-to-service APIs: smaller surface area encouraged, still documented with contract tests.
  - Streaming endpoints: use chunked transfer or HTTP/2 streams with a documented schema.
- Versioning and compatibility:
  - Major versioning via URL (/v1/) for breaking changes.
  - Backwards-compatible changes are minor versions and negotiated with consumers.
  - Deprecation policy: At least 90 days notice for public APIs; 30 days for internal unless critical.
- Authentication and authorization:
  - All APIs must authenticate requests using our centralized token service (JWT with short TTL for internal calls, API keys scoped for external clients).
  - RBAC-checks for privileged endpoints; sensitive actions require explicit audit logging.
- Error handling and codes:
  - Use standard HTTP semantics; include machine-readable error payload with `code`, `message`, and optional `details`.
  - Retryable transient errors must use 429/503 with Retry-After header.
- Pagination, filtering, and rate limits:
  - Cursor-based pagination preferred for large result sets.
  - Allow filtering and sorting via query params; validate inputs and include explicit limits for maximum page sizes.
  - Per-route rate limits are configured in the gateway and declared in the API spec.
- Contract testing and CI:
  - OpenAPI spec must be checked into repo and validated in CI.
  - Consumer contract tests (PACT or OpenAPI-driven) for public and cross-team integrations.
- Example snippet (OpenAPI):
  ---
  openapi: 3.1.0
  info:
    title: Example Service API
    version: 1.0.0
  paths:
    /generate:
      post:
        summary: Generate text
        security: - apiKey: []
        requestBody:
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/GenerateRequest'
  ---

SLOs / performance expectations for APIs:
- Customer-facing inference endpoints: availability 99.95% monthly; P95 latency <= 300ms for short prompts (<= 128 tokens) in hosted tier.
- Internal control-plane APIs: availability 99.9%; P95 latency <= 150ms.

2) Coding Standards
- Languages and supported stacks:
  - Backend: Go 1.21+ (preferred for runtime-critical services), Python 3.11+ (data/ML tooling), TypeScript (front-end and admin services).
- Style and linters:
  - Enforce gofmt/govet + staticcheck for Go; black/ruff + mypy for Python; eslint + prettier for TypeScript.
- Testing requirements:
  - Unit tests: >= 80% of new code paths covered (teams may set higher targets for critical components).
  - Integration: smoke tests for service surface.
  - E2E: gating for customer-facing features.
- PR reviews and CI gating:
  - Minimum two reviewers for changes to platform or shared libraries; at least one reviewer from owning service for service-level changes.
  - PR size guidance: keep < 300 LOC where possible; large changes must have design doc link in PR.
- Dependency management and reproducibility:
  - Dependabot/renovate for routine updates; critical dependency updates require security review.
  - Lockfiles required and reproducible build artifacts in CI.

3) Infrastructure Standards (IaC, networking, secrets)
- IaC and modules:
  - Terraform v1.5+ with canonical modules stored in `infra-modules` repo.
  - Module contract: variables documented, outputs typed, and all state in remote backend (consul/terraform cloud).
- Environment topology and parity:
  - Environments: dev, staging, preprod, prod. Keep configs as similar as feasible; differences documented in environment matrix.
- Networking and tenancy:
  - Standard VPC layout, subnets, and cross-account roles for prod access. Use service mesh for inter-service mTLS.
- Secrets and key management:
  - KMS for encryption at rest; secrets stored in Vault (or cloud secret manager) with automatic rotation policies.
- Capacity planning and tagging:
  - Resources tagged with team, service, cost-center, and environment.
  - Capacity plans: SRE to publish quarterly GPU capacity forecast and reservation guidance.

4) Model-Serving Standards
- Model packaging and metadata:
  - Models must include manifest metadata: model id, version, architecture, tokenizer version, quantization profile, input/output schema, and provenance (source and training data summary).
- Validation and quality gates:
  - Automated unit tests for tokenizer round-trips and sample inference outputs.
  - Evaluation harness must include perf benchmarks, safety filters, and regression tests against a canonical prompt set.
- Quantization and performance profiles:
  - Recommended quantization profiles stored under `confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles`; runtime must declare supported quantization flags.
- KV cache and runtime considerations:
  - KV cache correctness tests required; eviction policy defined per-model based on expected sequence length distribution.
- Rollout strategy and fallback:
  - Canary rollout (5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%) with automated quality checks at each stage.
  - Fallback policy: automatic fallback to compatible smaller/quantized model if SLOs degrade beyond threshold.
- Operational controls:
  - Throttles, request shaping, and prefix-caching options must be configurable per-route.

5) Observability Standards
- Metrics (Prometheus):
  - Required metrics for services: request_count (labels: route, method, result), request_latency_seconds (histogram with buckets tuned for target latency), tokens_generated_total (for inference endpoints), model_version_in_use, gpu_utilization_percent.
  - Export metrics with stable names and semantic labels.
- Tracing (OpenTelemetry):
  - Trace every request-level operation across the control plane and runtime where feasible; record model id, route, and request id as trace attributes.
- Logging:
  - Structured logs (JSON) with consistent fields: timestamp, level, service, env, request_id, trace_id, user_id (if applicable), message, and extra.
  - Sensitive fields must be redacted at the source.
- Dashboards and runbooks:
  - Per-service dashboards: latency heatmap, error rate, throughput, and top error classes.
  - Runbooks linked from dashboards and maintained as part of the service repo.
- Alerting thresholds (examples):
  - P99 latency > 2x target for 5m -> SEV2.
  - Error rate delta > 0.5% absolute over baseline for 10m -> SEV2.
  - Service availability below SLO window (see SLO section) -> Pager.

6) Performance Standards and Benchmarking
- Benchmark suite and cadence:
  - Runtime and model teams maintain a canonical perf-suite under `eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite`.
  - Full perf run on major infra changes and model onboarding; nightly synthetic smoke-run for regressions.
- Latency and throughput targets (examples):
  - Hosted small-prompt P95 <= 300ms, P99 <= 1s (depends on model class).
  - Dedicated GPU throughput guidance: target tokens/sec per GPU for common model families documented in perf matrix.
- Load testing and realistic workloads:
  - Use recorded production traffic traces for load generation where privacy allows; otherwise use representative synthetic mixes.
- Performance regression detection:
  - Each PR that touches runtime or model path must include a perf sanity check; CI should block on >10% regression for targeted microbenchmarks.

7) ADR (Architecture Decision Record) Process
- ADR template (required fields):
  - Title, status (proposed | accepted | deprecated), context, decision, consequences, date, authors, reviewers.
- Storing ADRs:
  - ADRs are stored in `confluence/architecture-and-standards` and linked from service repos. File name: `adr-YYYY-MM-DD-short-title.md` or `.json` where required.
- Approval workflow:
  - Proposed ADRs: authored + one platform lead reviewer.
  - Acceptance: sign-off from service owner, platform lead, and security if infra/data change.
- Example ADR topics: API versioning strategy, model quantization contract, region-based routing policy.

8) Compliance, Security, and Exceptions
- All infra changes touching data residency, KMS, or audit logging must route through security review.
- Exceptions to standards require a documented ADR or an approved risk-and-exceptions ticket filed with Security.

9) Onboarding and operational checklists
- New service checklist (high-level):
  1. Create OpenAPI / contract spec and register it.
  2. Include metrics, tracing, and structured logging hooks.
  3. Add Terraform module and tagging.
  4. Write runbook and link dashboards.
  5. Define SLOs and error budgets; register with SRE.

Appendix A — ADR template (text)
- Title: Short descriptive name
- Status: proposed | accepted | deprecated
- Date: YYYY-MM-DD
- Context: Why are we considering this?
- Decision: What we decided to do (concise)
- Consequences: Operational, cost, migration, rollback impacts
- Authors: list
- Reviewers: list

Appendix B — Example OpenAPI snippet and error schema
- See API Standards section above for minimal example. Error schema: { "code": "string", "message": "string", "details": ["string"] }

Notes and next steps:
- This canonical doc will be referenced by repo-level CONTRIBUTING.md and PR templates.
- Next review scheduled: 2026-06-01 or on-demand for major platform changes.
